mainTopic: רבא refuted about the תמורה of a lost פסח; שמואל's rule matching פסח to חטאת, its limits (lost animals only, following רבי), and the challenges to it.
overview: This amud opens at the end of a ברייתא that the גמרא uses against רבא. The ברייתא says that in a 'before the פסח' case, the תמורה of a lost פסח is not offered. The obvious reading would make the פסוק unnecessary. So the ברייתא must mean an animal found before the שחיטה and swapped after it, and רבא is refuted. Next, שמואל gives a rule: where a חטאת would die, a פסח becomes a שלמים, and where a חטאת would graze, a פסח grazes too. רבי יוחנן says instead that a פסח becomes a שלמים only if it was found after the שחיטה. רב יוסף challenges שמואל from an animal whose year has passed, and the answer is that שמואל meant only lost animals. A further challenge from the חכמים is answered by saying that שמואל follows רבי, for whom every lost חטאת dies. A פסח lost before midday does not count as lost, following רבא. The amud ends by asking how, according to רבי, a חטאת could ever graze, and the answer comes on the next amud.

steps.title: The ברייתא: A substitute of a פסח found 'before the פסח' is not offered
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא ends by teaching from the word 'הוא' that, in the 'before the פסח' case, the תמורה of the פסח is not offered.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might think the same is true even 'before the פסח.' So the פסוק says 'it': 'it' is offered, but the substitute of the פסח is not offered.
steps.whatsHappening: We are finishing a ברייתא that the גמרא quoted to challenge רבא. It says that in a 'before the פסח' case, the תמורה of a פסח cannot be brought as a שלמים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, the ברייתא taught that a תמורה of a פסח can sometimes be brought as a שלמים. Now it limits that rule with the word 'הוא.' In the case of 'before the פסח,' the substitute is not offered. The גמרא will next work out exactly which case this means.

keyTerms.meaning: 'One might think' (introduces a mistaken idea the פסוק will rule out)
'The verse teaches' (introduces the source from the פסוק)
A substitute animal that someone tried to swap for a קרבן; it becomes holy too
Is offered on the מזבח

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a brand-new statement. It is the end of a ברייתא that started on the previous amud. The ברייתא is being used as a challenge against רבא.

phrases.english: One might think: even before the Pesach, it is the same?
phrases.notes: 'Before the פסח' means before the replacement פסח was slaughtered.

phrases.english: The verse teaches: 'It'
— 'it' is offered,
but the substitute of the Pesach is not offered.

steps.triggerLanguage: יָכוֹל אַף לִפְנֵי הַפֶּסַח כֵּן? תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the ברייתא that was quoted against רבא on the previous amud.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's ruling that a תמורה made after the שחיטה, of a פסח found before it, may be brought as a שלמים.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא says that in a 'before' case, the תמורה is not offered. If that 'before' case is רבא's case, he is contradicted.

steps.title: What case is the ברייתא talking about?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what exact case the ברייתא's 'before the פסח' refers to.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what situation the ברייתא means. This is a setup line: it prepares a test of the possible readings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Before' could mean different things. It could refer to when the lost animal was found, or to when the swap was made. The answer will decide whether רבא is contradicted.

keyTerms.meaning: 'What is the case?' (asks for the exact situation)

phrases.english: What are the circumstances?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks which case the ברייתא's ruling covers.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether 'before the פסח' refers to the finding, the swap, or both.

steps.title: It can't mean found and swapped before the slaughter
steps.stepSummary: If both the finding and the swap happened before the slaughter, the rule is obvious, so the פסוק would not be needed for it.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say it means the animal was found before the slaughter and swapped before the slaughter, that is obvious! Why would I need a verse?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tests the first possible reading and rejects it. A פסוק is not needed to teach something obvious.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If everything happened before the replacement was slaughtered, the original animal was still a regular פסח when it was swapped. Its תמורה would clearly not be offered, so the פסוק would teach nothing new. That means the ברייתא must be talking about a less obvious case.

keyTerms.meaning: 'If you say' (introduces a suggested reading)
He made a swap (a תמורה)
'It is obvious!'
'Why do I need a verse?'

phrases.english: If you say that it was found before the slaughter
and he made a substitution with it before the slaughter —
that is obvious!
Why do I need a verse?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the first possible answer to 'היכי דמי.'
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The reading that both the finding and the swap happened before the slaughter.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It would make the פסוק unnecessary, because the law in that case is obvious.

steps.title: So it must mean found before but swapped after — exactly רבא's case
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא must be talking about an animal found before the slaughter but swapped after it. That is רבא's case, and the ברייתא rules against him.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, isn't it a case where the animal was found before the slaughter, and he swapped it after the slaughter!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא concludes what the ברייתא must mean. That meaning matches רבא's case and contradicts his ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the obvious case is ruled out, the only sensible reading is: found before the slaughter, swapped after it. רבא said the תמורה in that case can be a שלמים. The ברייתא says it is not offered, which is a direct clash.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Rather, isn't it…?' (forces the remaining reading)
After the slaughter (of the replacement פסח)

phrases.english: Rather, is it not that it was found before the slaughter
and he made a substitution with it after the slaughter!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: With the obvious reading rejected, it lands on the reading that clashes with רבא.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's ruling about a תמורה made after the שחיטה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא, read correctly, says that this exact case is 'not offered.' רבא said it is offered as a שלמים.

steps.title: רבא is refuted
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא declares that רבא's view is refuted.
steps.simpleTranslation: The refutation of רבא is a refutation.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא ends this argument. רבא's view is rejected.
steps.deeperAnalysis: No answer is given for רבא. The ברייתא stands against him, so his ruling in this version is rejected.

keyTerms.meaning: A conclusive refutation

steps.whatToRemember: A פסח found before the replacement was slaughtered keeps that status. Even if it is swapped after the slaughter, its תמורה is not offered as a שלמים. רבא is refuted.

phrases.english: The refutation of Rava is a conclusive refutation.

steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבא's view is rejected. The תמורה in this case is not offered.

steps.title: שמואל's rule: פסח follows the חטאת
steps.stepSummary: שמואל: in any case where a חטאת is left to die, a פסח is offered as a שלמים. In any case where a חטאת grazes, a פסח also grazes.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל said: Whatever would make a חטאת die makes a פסח be offered as a שלמים. Whatever would make a חטאת graze makes a פסח graze too.
steps.whatsHappening: A new section begins. שמואל gives a general rule that matches the laws of an unusable פסח to the laws of an unusable חטאת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An unusable חטאת is handled in one of two ways. Sometimes it is left to die (מתה). Sometimes it is left to graze (רועה) until it gets a blemish, and the money from selling it goes to a נדבה. שמואל says that where a חטאת dies, a פסח becomes a שלמים, and where a חטאת grazes, a פסח grazes too.

keyTerms.meaning: A חטאת that is put away to die
Grazes until it gets a blemish, then is sold
Peace-offering
'Whatever…' (introduces a general rule)

steps.whyThisMatters: It gives one simple key for many cases of a lost or extra פסח: just check what would happen to a חטאת in the same situation.

phrases.english: Shmuel said:
Whatever, in a sin-offering, dies —
in a Paschal lamb, is offered as a peace-offering;
and whatever, in a sin-offering, grazes —
in a Paschal lamb, also grazes.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic after רבא is refuted.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Where a חטאת dies, a פסח is offered as a שלמים. Where a חטאת grazes, a פסח grazes.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: Only if found after the slaughter
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says a פסח becomes a שלמים only if it was found after the replacement was slaughtered, not before.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: A פסח is offered as a שלמים only if it was found after the slaughter. But if it was found before the slaughter, it is not.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן gives a different, narrower rule for when a lost פסח becomes a שלמים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יוחנן, the timing of the finding is what decides. If the lost פסח turns up after the replacement was slaughtered, it becomes a שלמים. If it turns up before, it never becomes a שלמים; it was 'pushed aside' while it was still a fit פסח.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Only…' (limits the rule)
Was found (the lost animal)

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yochanan said:
The Paschal lamb is not offered as a peace-offering
except when it was found after the slaughter,
but before the slaughter — no.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second view next to שמואל's rule.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A פסח becomes a שלמים only if it was found after the שחיטה of the replacement.

steps.title: רב יוסף: Is that really a rule? A year-old חטאת grazes
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף challenges שמואל: a חטאת whose year has passed goes to graze, but a פסח whose year has passed becomes a שלמים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף objected: Is that a firm rule? What about a חטאת whose year has passed, which goes to graze?
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף attacks שמואל's rule by pointing to a case where the חטאת and the פסח do not match.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A חטאת past its first year goes to graze. By שמואל's rule, a פסח past its first year should graze too. But we know a פסח שעברה שנתו is offered as a שלמים, so the rule does not hold.

keyTerms.meaning: 'He strongly objected to it'
A general rule
Whose (first) year has passed
'Goes to grazing'

phrases.english: Rav Yosef objected to it:
And is it a general rule?
But there is a sin-offering whose year has passed,
which goes to grazing,

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַב יוֹסֵף: וּכְלָלָא הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to challenge שמואל's rule.
steps.kashyaTarget: The second half of שמואל's rule: whatever grazes in a חטאת also grazes in a פסח.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A year-old חטאת grazes, but a year-old פסח is offered as a שלמים. So the חטאת and פסח do not always match.

steps.title: Proof from ריש לקיש: A year-old חטאת is treated as if in a cemetery
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש teaches that a חטאת past its year is viewed as if it stands in a cemetery, so it goes to graze.
steps.simpleTranslation: As ריש לקיש said: A חטאת whose year has passed is viewed as if it is standing in a cemetery, and it grazes.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a source to prove that a year-old חטאת grazes. This backs up רב יוסף's challenge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A כהן cannot go into a cemetery to bring the animal, so it cannot be offered, yet it is not simply killed. It is sent to graze until it gets a blemish. This confirms that a year-old חטאת is in the 'grazing' group.

keyTerms.meaning: 'We view it as if…'
A cemetery

phrases.english: As Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish said:
A sin-offering whose year has passed —
we view it as though it were standing
in a cemetery,
and it grazes.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for רב יוסף's claim that a year-old חטאת grazes.
steps.raayaObject: That a חטאת שעברה שנתה goes to grazing.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The statement of ריש לקיש comparing it to an animal standing in a cemetery.

steps.title: A ברייתא shows that a פסח past its year is offered as a שלמים
steps.stepSummary: The second half of רב יוסף's challenge: a ברייתא proves that a פסח whose year has passed becomes a שלמים, while a חטאת in the same situation grazes.
steps.simpleTranslation: But a פסח in this same situation is offered as a שלמים. A ברייתא teaches this from the verse 'If a lamb': a פסח whose year has passed, and a שלמים that comes because of a פסח, follow all the laws of a שלמים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא completes רב יוסף's challenge from Step 8 by bringing a source for the פסח side of the comparison.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 9 proved that a חטאת past its year goes to graze. This ברייתא proves that a פסח past its year is brought as a שלמים, with all the laws of a שלמים. So in the very same case the two animals end up differently, which contradicts שמואל's rule that they always match.

keyTerms.meaning: Whose year has passed: the animal is now older than one year, the age limit for a פסח
The fat tail of a sheep, which is burned on the מזבח
Leaning one's hands on the animal before it is slaughtered
Wine and flour offerings that are brought with a קרבן
Waving the breast and thigh of the animal
The verse interrupted the topic, starting a new subject

steps.confusionAlert: Most of the ברייתא deals with side details, such as the fat tail and the goat. The only part that matters for this argument is that a פסח whose year has passed is treated as a full שלמים.

phrases.english: Whereas with a Paschal lamb in a case like this
it is offered as a peace-offering
as it was taught: "A lamb"
comes to include the Paschal lamb regarding the fat tail
When it says: "If a lamb"
it comes to include a Paschal lamb whose year has passed
and peace-offerings that come because of a Paschal lamb
in all the laws of peace-offerings
that they require leaning and libations
and the waving of the breast and thigh
When it says: "If a goat"
it interrupted the topic

phrases.aramaic: לִימֵּד עַל הָעֵז שֶׁאֵין טָעוּן אַלְיָה
phrases.english: to teach about the goat that it does not require the fat tail

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִילּוּ בְּפֶסַח כִּי הַאי גַוְונָא קָרֵב שְׁלָמִים, דְּתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source for the פסח side of the challenge, matching Step 9, which supplied the source for the חטאת side.
steps.raayaObject: That a פסח whose year has passed is offered as a שלמים.

steps.title: שמואל's rule applies only to lost animals
steps.stepSummary: The answer: שמואל was speaking only about lost animals, not about animals pushed off because they became unfit.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: When שמואל said his rule, he meant animals that were lost. He did not say it about animals that were pushed off.
steps.whatsHappening: The challenge is answered by narrowing שמואל's rule so that it does not cover the case of an animal whose year has passed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An animal whose year has passed is a דחוי. It was not lost; it was pushed off because it can no longer be used for its original purpose. שמואל's matching rule was only about אבודין, animals that went missing. So the year-passed case does not contradict him.

keyTerms.meaning: Animals that were lost and later found
Animals that were pushed off, meaning disqualified from their original use

phrases.english: He said to him
When Shmuel said it, it was regarding lost animals
regarding deferred animals he did not say it

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Steps 8 to 10.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the scope of the rule
steps.terutzHavaAmina: שמואל's rule covers every case where a חטאת grazes or dies, including a disqualified animal.
steps.terutzMaskana: The rule covers only lost animals, so the year-passed case is outside it.

steps.title: Even for lost animals, the rule seems to fail
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the narrowed rule: according to the חכמים, a חטאת that was lost when its replacement was set aside goes to graze.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does the rule even work for lost animals? Take a חטאת that was lost at the time its replacement was set aside. According to the חכמים, it goes to graze.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer from Step 11 by asking whether שמואל's rule really holds even for lost animals. It begins with the חטאת side of the comparison.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under the narrowed rule, a lost חטאת and a lost פסח should match. But the חכמים hold that a lost חטאת found before atonement grazes, rather than dies. Steps 13 and 14 will show that the source supports this and that the פסח does not match.

keyTerms.meaning: Do you really find it so? A challenging question
At the time the replacement animal was set aside
Grazing: left to pasture until it gets a blemish, then sold

phrases.english: And regarding a lost one, do you find it so?
But there is one lost at the time of separation
according to the Rabbis, which goes to grazing

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָבוּד מִי מַשְׁכַּחַתְּ לַהּ? וַהֲרֵי אֲבוּדָה בִּשְׁעַת הַפְרָשָׁה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer given in Step 11.
steps.kashyaTarget: The narrowed version of שמואל's rule, which applies only to lost animals.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A lost חטאת grazes according to the חכמים, so the matching פסח should graze too. Step 14 shows that it does not.

steps.title: The משנה about a lost חטאת and its replacement
steps.stepSummary: A משנה records a dispute. רבי says one animal is offered and the other dies. The חכמים say the חטאת dies only if it is found after atonement, so before atonement it grazes.
steps.simpleTranslation: Someone set aside a חטאת and it got lost. He set aside another in its place, and then the first was found, so now both are there. רבי says one is offered and the other dies. The חכמים say a חטאת dies only if it is found after the owner already got atonement. So if it is found before atonement, it grazes.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the משנה that proves the claim in Step 12 about the חכמים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי holds that a lost-and-found חטאת is left to die no matter when it is found. The חכמים say it dies only if it is found after atonement. The inference from their words, introduced by הא, is that a חטאת found earlier grazes, and that is the case the challenge relies on.

keyTerms.meaning: It shall die: left alone without food until it dies
The owners already got atonement through the other animal
This implies: an inference drawn from the wording

steps.confusionAlert: Be careful about which animal is which. The 'first' one is the original that was lost and then found. The 'second' is the replacement.

phrases.english: As we learned: If one separated his sin-offering and it was lost
and he separated another in its place
and the first was found
and both are now standing
one of them is offered
and the second shall die; these are the words of Rabbi
And the Rabbis say
a sin-offering is not left to die
unless it was found after the owners gained atonement
this implies that before the owners gained atonement, it grazes

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Provides the source for the claim in Step 12.
steps.raayaObject: According to the חכמים, a lost חטאת found before atonement grazes.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A משנה recording the dispute between רבי and the חכמים.

steps.title: A lost פסח found before slaughter becomes a שלמים
steps.stepSummary: The challenge is completed: a lost פסח found after midday but before slaughter is offered as a שלמים, so it does not graze the way the חטאת does.
steps.simpleTranslation: But a פסח that was lost and then found after midday, before the slaughter, is offered as a שלמים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the challenge by giving the פסח side, which does not match the חטאת side from Step 13.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to the חכמים, the lost חטאת grazes. If שמואל's rule were true, the matching lost פסח should also graze. Instead it is brought as a שלמים, so the rule fails even for lost animals.

keyTerms.meaning: After midday on ערב פסח, when the time to slaughter the פסח begins
Before the replacement פסח was slaughtered

phrases.english: Whereas with a Paschal lamb
where it was lost and then found
after midday, before the slaughter
it is offered as a peace-offering

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the challenge begun in Step 12 by giving the contrasting פסח case.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's rule as applied to lost animals.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The חטאת grazes but the פסח becomes a שלמים, so the two do not match.

steps.title: שמואל follows רבי, who holds that a lost חטאת dies
steps.stepSummary: The answer: שמואל agrees with רבי that a lost חטאת is always left to die. So a lost פסח, which matches it, becomes a שלמים.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל holds like רבי, who said that a lost חטאת goes to death.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא resolves the challenge by saying that שמואל follows רבי, not the חכמים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבי, every lost חטאת dies, even one found before atonement. Under שמואל's rule, a dying חטאת matches a פסח that becomes a שלמים, and that is exactly what happens to the lost פסח. So the contradiction disappears.

keyTerms.meaning: He holds, meaning this is his opinion
It goes to death

steps.whatToRemember: שמואל's matching rule between חטאת and פסח has two limits. First, it applies only to lost animals, not to animals pushed off as unfit. Second, it follows רבי, who holds that any lost חטאת is left to die.

phrases.english: Shmuel holds in accordance with Rabbi
who said a lost one goes to death

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Steps 12 to 14.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Assigning the view to a particular תנא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: שמואל follows the חכמים, so a lost חטאת would graze.
steps.terutzMaskana: שמואל follows רבי, so a lost חטאת dies, which matches the פסח becoming a שלמים.

steps.title: A פסח lost and found before midday grazes
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the answer of step 15. For רבי every lost חטאת dies, yet a פסח lost and found before midday grazes. That breaks the match שמואל's rule needs.
steps.simpleTranslation: But according to רבי, every lost חטאת is left to die. Yet with a פסח that was lost before midday and found before midday, it grazes!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer it just gave, that שמואל follows רבי. It points to a פסח case that does not fit that pattern.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 15 we said that for רבי a lost חטאת always dies, so a matching lost פסח should become a שלמים. But there is a case where a lost פסח simply grazes: it was lost before midday and found before midday. If 'lost' always means 'dies' for רבי, this grazing פסח has no matching חטאת rule.

keyTerms.meaning: A lost animal (here, a lost חטאת)
It dies (it is locked away until it dies)
Midday on ערב פסח, when the time for offering the פסח begins
It grazes (it is left until it gets a blemish, then sold)
Whereas, but in contrast

steps.confusionAlert: Keep the two outcomes apart. 'Dies' means the animal is left to die. 'Grazes' means it pastures until it gets a blemish and is then redeemed. They are different results.

phrases.english: But every lost one, according to Rabbi, dies,
phrases.notes: Refers to a lost חטאת, as stated in step 15.

phrases.english: whereas with a Pesach,
where it was lost before midday
and found before midday, it grazes!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 15, that שמואל follows רבי.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that שמואל follows רבי, for whom every lost חטאת dies.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A lost פסח found before midday grazes, which does not match a חטאת that always dies. So the match between the two breaks down.

steps.title: Before midday the פסח does not count as lost
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that a פסח lost before midday does not count as lost. This follows רבא's rule that something lost at night is not called lost.
steps.simpleTranslation: Before midday it is not considered lost. This follows רבא, who said: something lost at night is not called lost.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. The before-midday case is not a lost-animal case at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא taught that a חטאת lost at night is not called lost, because it could not be offered at night anyway. In the same way, a פסח cannot be offered before midday, so losing it then does not give it the status of a lost animal. רבי's rule that lost animals die does not apply here, so grazing does not contradict it.

keyTerms.meaning: Something lost at night, when it could not be offered anyway
It is not called lost (it does not get lost-animal status)
In line with the view of רבא

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up a key principle. Something counts as legally 'lost' only if it went missing at a time when it could have been used.

phrases.english: Before midday, it is not lost,
in line with Rava, for Rava said:
something lost at night is not called lost.
phrases.notes: It could not be offered at night anyway. The same is true of a פסח before midday.

steps.triggerLanguage: קוֹדֶם חֲצוֹת לָאו אָבוּד הוּא, כִּדְרָבָא
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the case: the before-midday case is not a 'lost' case at all.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A פסח lost before midday is a lost animal, so for רבי it should match a חטאת that dies.
steps.terutzMaskana: Following רבא, a loss at a time when the animal could not be offered anyway is not a legal loss. So the grazing פסח falls outside רבי's rule that lost animals die.

steps.title: For רבי, when does a sin-offering ever graze?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא raises a new problem. If for רבי every lost חטאת dies, when would a חטאת ever graze? If it never does, the grazing half of שמואל's rule seems to have no case.
steps.simpleTranslation: But then, according to רבי, how can you find a case of a חטאת that grazes?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a new problem with saying שמואל follows רבי. The answer comes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל's rule also speaks about a חטאת that grazes and matches it to a פסח. But if רבי holds that every lost חטאת dies, there seems to be no grazing חטאת at all according to him. Then that half of שמואל's rule would have nothing to refer to.

keyTerms.meaning: How can you find such a case?
But then, if so

phrases.english: But then, a grazing one, according to Rabbi,
phrases.notes: A חטאת that is left to graze.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on steps 15 and 17. Since for רבי every lost חטאת dies, it asks whether a grazing חטאת can exist for him.
